question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw-authored external-content wrappers by default, expose an operator `captureFilter` option, or defer this narrow filter to the broader provenance/trust architecture?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent boundary determines whether OpenClaw enforces wrapper trust by default or delegates it to configuration, which is a product/security decision.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for web, browser, and tool-wrapped content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented operator-controlled `excludeWrapped` option with schema, manifest, docs, and default/upgrade behavior tests.

options.title: Defer to provenance design
options.body: Keep this narrow issue open until the broader memory trust and durable provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for web, browser, and tool-wrapped content.
